clue.text: In fog walk around London landmark

indicators.note: around says the walk word is wrapped about the fog word

parts.note: to march is to walk in step
blear means dim or misty, as if seen in fog

explanation.surface: Someone strolls about in the fog near a famous London sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fog' is not an insertion signal: it is the fog word itself, blear meaning misty. The landmark is the triumphal arch at the north-east corner of Hyde Park.
explanation.definitionFit: The arch at the north-east corner of Hyde Park is one of London's best-known monuments.

clue.text: Acceptance of a Democrat by election

parts.note: election in its older sense of choosing, an option

explanation.surface: A Democrat is accepted after winning a vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'election' looks political, but here it means a choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption of a proposal is its acceptance or taking up.

clue.text: Seeing snake, wild animal runs away

indicators.note: away says the runs letter goes from the animal word

parts.note: a boar is a wild pig
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: On seeing a snake, a wild beast flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs away' reads as one phrase about fleeing; split it into R (runs) and the deletion signal 'away'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boa is a large constricting serpent.

clue.text: Some declare a sesame oil relaxes

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone claims that sesame oil helps them unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the last letter of 'declare', takes 'a', and the first three letters of 'sesame'.
explanation.definitionFit: To oil something makes it run smoothly, so it relaxes or loosens it.

clue.text: Badge worn as a favour

definitions.meaning: a ribbon badge awarded at shows or worn at elections
a favour is a ribbon or knot worn to show support

explanation.surface: A badge is pinned on as a token of loyalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon rosette serves both as an award badge and as a supporter's favour.

clue.text: Trouble afoot as home team's beaten, with resistance overcome

indicators.note: overcome means covered over, so the resistance letter is enclosed by the scrambled letters
beaten, as in eggs beaten up, says the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the words home team, the possessive adding no letter
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Fans are troubled when the home side loses, despite putting up a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' turns HOMETEAM into HAMMETOE, and 'overcome' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hammer toe is a deformed, bent toe, literally a trouble of the foot.

clue.text: Burn, as it is hot in vehicle

indicators.note: in says the hot letter sits inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A car gets scorched because it is hot inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To char something is to scorch or burn its surface.

clue.text: Says right chisel is needed to break hard cases

indicators.note: breaking the words up signals that their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone insists a chisel is the right tool for cracking tough shells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is only a link here. Pupae's hard cases are chrysalises.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrysalises are the hard protective casings of insect pupae.

clue.text: A3 road is short in a car

parts.note: a cross-reference to the answer of 3 down, a snake
Rd is the short form of road

explanation.surface: Read as a motorist's complaint about a short stretch of the A3 road.
explanation.walkthrough: The 3 is not part of the road number: it points to 3 down. The A3 is a major road from London to Portsmouth.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aboard is to be on or in a vehicle such as a car.

clue.text: Syrup used in a shake by girls

parts.note: in two shakes means in a moment, so a shake is a mo
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: A syrup is mixed into a milkshake by some young women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shake' suggests a milkshake, but it is a moment, informally a mo.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is the thick dark syrup left from refining sugar.

clue.text: Reddish-brown desert

definitions.meaning: to abandon them, as on an island

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a brownish-crimson colour and the act of abandoning someone.

clue.text: Punishment for bands that hold up ships

definitions.meaning: the ... were a wooden frame in which offenders were pilloried
a stock is a stiff band of cloth worn round the neck
the timber framework supporting a ship while it is built

explanation.definitionFit: Stocks names an old pillory, stiff neckbands, and the frame for building ships.

clue.text: Unexpected mishap parking in centre most clumsily

indicators.note: in says the parking letter goes inside the rearranged letters
done clumsily, the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: P is the map and road sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Parking right in the middle, badly, causes an unfortunate incident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clumsily' rearranges CENTREMOST to CONTRETEMS, and 'in' puts P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A contretemps is an unfortunate or embarrassing setback or minor clash.

clue.text: River estuary redefined in thesaurus

indicators.note: redefined suggests reshaping, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry for river estuary has been rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thesaurus' is the definition: a thesaurus is a treasury of words, which is what the Greek name means.
explanation.definitionFit: Thesaurus literally means a treasure-house, and a treasury is a store of valuable things.

clue.text: Business with a loss leader holding event at the same time

indicators.note: holding says the outer letters keep the event word between them

parts.note: Co is short for company, a business

indicators.note: the leader of the word loss is its first letter

parts.note: an incident is an event

explanation.surface: A firm sells at a loss to win custom, staging a promotion simultaneously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loss leader' is a sales term, but here 'leader' just picks L from 'loss'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coincidental events happen at the same time by chance, describing simultaneity.

clue.text: Panda perhaps carried by native bodily

indicators.note: carried by says the car word is held within the native word

parts.note: native in the sense of inborn, innate
a panda car is a British police car, so a car by example

explanation.surface: A giant panda is carried along by a local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panda' suggests the bear, but a panda car was a small British police patrol car.
explanation.definitionFit: Incarnate means embodied, in bodily form.

clue.text: Great lover has no alternative, as member of two unions

parts.note: big means great

indicators.note: has no says the alternative word is taken out of the lover word

parts.note: an amorist is a lover
or is the word that introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A great lover lacks other options.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove OR from AMORIST to leave AMIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigamist is married to two people at once, a member of two unions.

clue.text: Property manager's office has joint fences in front

indicators.note: in front says the fences word is placed before the joint word

parts.note: a fence is a receiver of stolen goods
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: A dodgy bar has fences standing out at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fences' looks like garden barriers but means dealers in stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Receivership is the office of a receiver who manages an insolvent's property.

clue.text: They show the power that numbers possess

definitions.text: They show the power that numbers possess

parts.words: They show the power that numbers possess
parts.note: the power reads as might, but in maths small raised figures say what power a number is raised to

explanation.definitionFit: Indices, or exponents, show the power to which numbers are raised.

clue.text: One who puts up with a native servant

definitions.meaning: one who bears or tolerates something
in British India a ... was a household servant

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both someone who tolerates or carries, and a colonial-era Indian servant.

clue.text: Reconstructed fund in debt

indicators.note: in says the fund word goes inside the debt word

parts.note: being in the red means in debt
a store is a fund or stock

explanation.surface: A fund that was in debt has been rebuilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something restored has been rebuilt or brought back to its former state.

clue.text: Invest in institute

definitions.meaning: to invest someone is to install them formally in office
to institute a cleric is to install them in a benefice

explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean placing someone formally in an office, which is what installing does.

clue.text: Bone found in ancient Troy

definitions.meaning: the broad upper bone of the pelvis

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a hip bone and also the classical city of Troy.

clue.text: Peninsula's edge is in mid-ocean

indicators.note: is in says the edge word sits inside the other letters
mid- picks out the middle letters of ocean

parts.note: a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A peninsula's coastline lies in the middle of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peninsula's' reads as 'the peninsula is', so the whole word is the definition; 'mid-ocean' takes the middle three letters of the five-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimea is a peninsula jutting into the Black Sea.

clue.text: Cook, one with erratic standards

indicators.note: to cook figures is to rework them, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chef with inconsistent quality standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a noun, but here it is a verb, as in cooking the books.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are standards by which something is judged.

clue.text: When one is due a letter

definitions.meaning: the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.definitionFit: The letters stand for estimated time of arrival and also spell a Greek alphabet character.

clue.text: Where batsman stands, we hear, showing blade

indicators.note: we hear says the word is said out loud

parts.note: in cricket the batsman stands at the crease, the line marked by the stumps

explanation.surface: A cricketer at his post brandishes a sword.
explanation.walkthrough: The crease is the line in cricket where the batter takes guard; a kris is a Malay dagger, said like 'crease'.
explanation.definitionFit: A kris is a Malay or Indonesian dagger with a wavy blade.

clue.text: Sea-dogs on the town needing a purge

indicators.note: on says the sailors are placed after the town

parts.note: Epsom is a town in Surrey, famous for its racecourse
old salts are seasoned sailors, sea-dogs

explanation.surface: Sailors out on the town need clearing out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the town' suggests a night out; here the sailors come after the town. Epsom salts are magnesium sulphate, taken as a laxative.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom salts are a traditional laxative, used to purge the bowels.
